## Data Preparation

```{r}
library(haven)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)

efcu <- read_sav("Case 31 Data_efcu_4.sav")

dim(efcu)
names(efcu)
```

## R1: Reasons for Joining the Credit Union

### Descriptive Statistics

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r1-descriptive
#| tbl-cap: "Distribution of Members' Opinions on Savings Interest Rates"

attr(efcu$q7, "labels")

table(efcu$q7, useNA = "ifany")

round(prop.table(table(efcu$q7)) * 100, 2)
```

## R1: One-Sample t-test

```{r}
q7_valid <- as.numeric(efcu$q7)
q7_valid <- q7_valid[q7_valid %in% 1:5]

mean(q7_valid)
sd(q7_valid)

t.test(q7_valid, mu = 3)
```

## R1: Savings Interest Rate Perceptions

```{r}
#| label: fig-r1-rates
#| fig-cap: "Members' Perceptions of Savings Interest Rates"

r1_data <- data.frame(
  Rating = factor(
    q7_valid,
    levels = 1:5,
    labels = c("Very High", "High", "Average",
               "Low", "Very Low")
  )
)

ggplot(r1_data, aes(x = Rating)) +
  geom_bar(
    aes(y = after_stat(count / sum(count) * 100)),
    fill = "steelblue"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Interest Rate Rating",
    y = "Percentage (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## R1: Findings and Insights

As shown in @fig-r1-rates, most members (70.34%) perceived the credit union's savings interest rates as average, while 18.64% rated them as high and 11.02% rated them as low or very low.

The average rating was not significantly different from the midpoint of 3 (M = 2.93, SD = 0.57, t(117) = -1.30, p = .196).

These findings suggest that savings interest rates may not be a strong competitive advantage for attracting new members. However, Q7 measures rate perceptions rather than actual reasons for joining.

```{r}
q8_valid <- as.numeric(efcu$Q8_r)

mean(q8_valid)
sd(q8_valid)
```

```{r}
mean(q30_valid)

```

## R2: Loan Rate Perceptions

```{r}
#| label: fig-r2-loan-rates
#| fig-cap: "Members' Perceptions of Credit Union Loan Rates"

r2_data <- data.frame(
  Rating = factor(
    q8_valid,
    levels = 1:5,
    labels = c("Very Low", "Low", "Average",
               "High", "Very High")
  )
)

ggplot(r2_data, aes(x = Rating)) +
  geom_bar(
    aes(y = after_stat(count / sum(count) * 100)),
    fill = "steelblue"
  ) +
  labs(x = "Loan Rate Rating", y = "Percentage (%)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## R2: Loan Rates Compared to Competitors

```{r}
#| label: fig-r2-competitors
#| fig-cap: "Agreement That Credit Union Loan Rates Are Lower"

r2_comp <- data.frame(
  Rating = factor(
    q30_valid,
    levels = 1:5,
    labels = c("Strongly Disagree", "Disagree",
               "Uncertain", "Agree", "Strongly Agree")
  )
)

ggplot(r2_comp, aes(x = Rating)) +
  geom_bar(
    aes(y = after_stat(count / sum(count) * 100)),
    fill = "steelblue"
  ) +
  labs(x = "Agreement Level", y = "Percentage (%)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1))
```

## R2: Findings and Insights

As shown in @fig-r2-loan-rates, 55.14% of members perceived the credit union's loan rates as average, while 28.04% rated them as high or very high.

As shown in @fig-r2-competitors, 46.09% of members were uncertain whether the credit union offered lower loan rates than its competitors.

Neither loan rate perceptions (M = 3.14, t(106) = 1.91, p = .058) nor agreement about lower loan rates (M = 3.06, t(127) = 0.82, p = .416) differed significantly from the midpoint.

## R2: Recommendations

These findings suggest that the credit union could improve communication about its loan rates and competitive advantages. However, the results do not directly establish why members borrow from other financial institutions.

```{r}
r5_vars <- paste0("q", 13:26, "_r")

attr(efcu$q13_r, "labels")

lapply(efcu[r5_vars[1:7]], function(x) {
  table(x, useNA = "ifany")
})
```

## R5: Descriptive Statistics — Q20–Q26

```{r}
lapply(efcu[r5_vars[8:14]], function(x) {
  table(x, useNA = "ifany")
})
```

## R5: Recoding Verification

```{r}
attr(efcu$q13, "label")
attr(efcu$q13, "labels")

table(
  Original = efcu$q13,
  Recoded = efcu$q13_r,
  useNA = "ifany"
)
```

## R5: Summary of Service Awareness

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r5-awareness
#| tbl-cap: "Response Distribution Across Credit Union Services"

r5_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(r5_vars, function(v) {
  counts <- table(factor(efcu[[v]], levels = 1:3))

  data.frame(
    Question = v,
Unaware = as.integer(counts[1]),
Aware_Not_Used = as.integer(counts[2]),
Aware_Used = as.integer(counts[3]),
    Total = sum(counts)
  )
}))

kable(r5_summary)
```

```{r}
#| include: false

sapply(13:26, function(i) {
  original <- as.numeric(efcu[[paste0("q", i)]])
  recoded <- as.numeric(efcu[[paste0("q", i, "_r")]])

  all(recoded == 4 - original, na.rm = TRUE)
})
```

## R5: Chi-Square Goodness-of-Fit Test

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r5-chisquare
#| tbl-cap: "Chi-Square Test Results for Service Awareness"

r5_tests <- do.call(rbind, lapply(r5_vars, function(v) {

  counts <- table(factor(efcu[[v]], levels = 1:3))

  test <- chisq.test(counts, p = rep(1/3, 3))

  data.frame(
    Question = v,
    Chi_Square = round(as.numeric(test$statistic), 2),
    df = as.numeric(test$parameter),
    P_Value = format.pval(test$p.value, digits = 3, eps = 0.001),
    Significant = ifelse(test$p.value < 0.05, "Yes", "No")
  )
}))

kable(r5_tests)
```

## R5: Service Awareness and Usage

```{r}
#| label: fig-r5-awareness
#| fig-cap: "Awareness and Usage of Credit Union Services"
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6

r5_plot <- as.data.frame(
  as.table(as.matrix(r5_summary[, 2:4]))
)

names(r5_plot) <- c("Service", "Awareness", "Count")

r5_plot$Service <- factor(
  rep(paste0("Q", 13:26), 3),
  levels = rev(paste0("Q", 13:26))
)

r5_plot$Awareness <- factor(
  r5_plot$Awareness,
  levels = c("Unaware", "Aware_Not_Used", "Aware_Used"),
  labels = c("Unaware", "Aware but Not Used", "Aware and Used")
)

ggplot(r5_plot, aes(x = Service, y = Count, fill = Awareness)) +
  geom_col(position = "fill") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("gray70", "skyblue", "steelblue")) +
  labs(
    x = "Credit Union Services",
    y = "Percentage (%)",
    fill = "Awareness Level"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## R5: Findings and Insights

As shown in @fig-r5-awareness, awareness and usage patterns vary across the 14 credit union services.

All 14 chi-square goodness-of-fit tests were statistically significant (p < .001), indicating that the response distributions differed significantly from an equal distribution.

For Q13, 64.84% of respondents were unaware of the service. In contrast, all respondents were aware of the service represented by Q26, although only 37.50% had used it.

## R5: Recommendations

The findings suggest that the credit union should increase awareness of less familiar services and encourage members to use services they already know about.



## R6: Data Recoding

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r6-recoding
#| tbl-cap: "Valid Responses for Q11 and Q12"

efcu$q11_r <- ifelse(
  efcu$q11 == 1, 2,
  ifelse(efcu$q11 == 2, 1, NA)
)

efcu$q12_r <- ifelse(
  efcu$q12 == 1, 2,
  ifelse(efcu$q12 == 2, 1, NA)
)

table(efcu$q11_r, useNA = "ifany")
table(efcu$q12_r, useNA = "ifany")
```

## R6: Chi-Square Goodness-of-Fit Test

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r6-chisquare
#| tbl-cap: "Chi-Square Tests for Operational Effectiveness"

r6_chi_vars <- c(
  "q9_r", "q10_r", "q11_r", "q12_r"
)

r6_levels <- list(1:5, 1:4, 1:2, 1:2)

r6_chi_tests <- do.call(rbind, lapply(
  seq_along(r6_chi_vars), function(i) {

    v <- r6_chi_vars[i]

    counts <- table(
      factor(efcu[[v]], levels = r6_levels[[i]])
    )

    test <- chisq.test(counts)

    data.frame(
      Question = v,
      N = sum(counts),
      Chi_Square = round(as.numeric(test$statistic), 2),
      df = as.numeric(test$parameter),
      P_Value = format.pval(test$p.value,
                            digits = 3, eps = 0.001),
      Significant = ifelse(test$p.value < 0.05,
                           "Yes", "No")
    )
  }
))

kable(r6_chi_tests)
```

## R6: One-Sample t-test

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r6-ttest
#| tbl-cap: "One-Sample t-tests for Operational Effectiveness"

r6_t_vars <- c(
  "q31", "q32", "q33", "q34", "Q37_r"
)

r6_t_tests <- do.call(rbind, lapply(r6_t_vars, function(v) {

  x <- as.numeric(efcu[[v]])
  x <- x[x %in% 1:5]

  test <- t.test(x, mu = 3)

  data.frame(
    Question = v,
    N = length(x),
    Mean = round(mean(x), 3),
    SD = round(sd(x), 3),
    t = round(as.numeric(test$statistic), 3),
    df = as.numeric(test$parameter),
    P_Value = format.pval(test$p.value,
                          digits = 3, eps = 0.001),
    Significant = ifelse(test$p.value < 0.05,
                         "Yes", "No")
  )
}))

kable(r6_t_tests)
```

## R6: Operational Effectiveness Ratings

```{r}
#| label: fig-r6-ratings
#| fig-cap: "Mean Ratings of Operational Effectiveness"

ggplot(r6_t_tests, aes(x = Question, y = Mean)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue", width = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 3,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "red"
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = round(Mean, 2)),
    vjust = -0.5
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 5),
    breaks = 0:5
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Survey Question",
    y = "Mean Rating"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
#| include: false

lapply(c("q31", "q32", "q33", "q34"), function(v) {
  list(
    Question = v,
    Description = attr(efcu[[v]], "label"),
    Labels = attr(efcu[[v]], "labels")
  )
})

table(Original = efcu$q9, Recoded = efcu$q9_r)
table(Original = efcu$q37, Recoded = efcu$Q37_r)
```

## R6: Findings and Interpretation

The chi-square goodness-of-fit tests for Q9, Q10, Q11,
and Q12 showed statistically significant differences
from equal response distributions (p < 0.001).

Approximately 77.3% of respondents reported that the
frequency of financial statements was about right.
Additionally, 97.7% indicated that the statements were
easy to understand, and 69.8% of valid respondents
believed that their account information was maintained
confidentially.

## R6: Findings — Operational Ratings

The one-sample t-tests showed that all five operational
effectiveness measures had mean ratings significantly
above the neutral midpoint of 3 (p < 0.001).

The overall management and operational rating received
the highest mean score (M = 4.066), while the simplicity
of loan applications received the lowest mean score
(M = 3.461).

Overall, respondents demonstrated positive perceptions
of the credit union's operational effectiveness.
However, simplifying loan applications and strengthening
confidence in account confidentiality may provide
opportunities for further improvement.
